correctness.rationale: The exact source identity \(v_\varepsilon=\mathcal K(\varepsilon(I-Q)N(u_\varepsilon))\) and odd homogeneity \(\mathcal K(\lambda h)=\operatorname{sgn}(\lambda)|\lambda|^{1/(p-1)}\mathcal K(h)\) give the signed two-sided limit for the zero-mean component. The source's local compactness argument gives \(u_\varepsilon\to\alpha\) for arbitrary local selections. Its derivative computation \(D_x(QN)(\alpha)\mathcal K(e-\bar e)=0\) makes the mean component \(o(|\varepsilon|^{1/(p-1)})\). If \(e-\bar e\neq0\), the right-inverse identity makes the leading profile nonzero, and since \(1/(p-1)<1\) the parameter difference quotient diverges. All quantifiers, signs, and norms were checked analytically; no finite experiment substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The result identifies the precise parameter-regularity boundary created by the nonlinear p-Laplacian inverse: solutions exist on both sides of zero, yet every local selection has the same signed fractional-power leading response and an infinite parameter difference quotient when the forcing oscillates. This turns the source's qualitative failure of linearization into an exact, selection-independent dynamical response law. It is a motivated boundary statement about continuation regularity, not a parameter renaming or a finite numerical slice.
